---
title: "select(-missing) fails, select(-matches(\"missing\")) stays quiet"
ref: TDY-05
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: incoherent
attendu: "the same behaviour for a column that does not exist"
versions: "All versions of {dplyr}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022)"
---

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

flowers <- head(iris, n = 2)
select(flowers, -Sepal.Lenght)
names(select(flowers, -matches("Sepal.Lenght")))
```
:::

## Why

A bare name must refer to an existing column: `select()` stops if it cannot find it. Helpers such as `matches()`, `starts_with()` or `contains()` return the set of matching columns, and an empty set is not an error. Removing "nothing" removes nothing.

A typo in a `matches()` thus goes unnoticed: the column you thought you had removed is still there.

## The remedy

Say what you mean: `all_of()` when the columns must exist, `any_of()` when they are optional.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

select(flowers, -all_of("Sepal.Lenght"))
names(select(flowers, -any_of(c("Sepal.Length", "optional_column"))))
```
:::
